Dear [Mr Craik](/person/379)
In a day or two you will receive from the [National Society](/organisation/32) a story of mine called [Grisly Grisell](/book/228). It was written for them, but has turned out too historical for their purpose, and as a tale was wanted to be coupled with [‘The Rubies of St Lo’](/book/234) I think it will serve the purpose. Mr [George Macmillan](/person/1946) knows all about the Rubies, which are in the Christmas number of the [Monthly Packet](/periodical/52).
Grisly Grisell is a variation on Sir Gawain’s ‘Loathly Lady’[^1]
[Miss Coleridge](/person/329) agrees to accept £100 between us for the copyright of ‘Strolling Players’. Really by far the best and most original part is hers. The idea was mine, but I did not know enough about theatricals to carry it out

Yours truly

C M Yonge


[^1]: The story of Sir Gawain and the Loathly Lady occurs in many versions of which the best known is perhaps Chaucer\'s \'Wife of Bath\'s Tale\'.
